question.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Stretch Transformation Given a Vector and its Image
question.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we are told that $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-component of $T(v)$ is $2$ times the $x$-component of $v,$ while

- the $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v)$ are the same.

So, we conclude that $T$ represents a stretch of scale factor $2$ in the $x$-direction. 

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

question.knowledge_point: Identifying a Shear or Stretch Transformation Represented by a Matrix
question.problem:
What linear transformation is represented by the following matrix
$[\begin{aligned}1 & 10 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can find the images of the standard basis vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of  $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 10 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ T(j) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 10 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=10i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix represents a *horizontal* shear with a shear factor of $10.$

question.problem:
What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the following matrix
$[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can find the images of the standard basis vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of  $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ T(j) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=5j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix represents a stretch of scale factor $5$ in the $y$-direction.

Let $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ What is the image of the square $R$ (shown above) under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Looking at the matrix $T$, we can see that $T$ represents a horizontal shear of shear factor $1.$ Therefore, the image of the square $R$ under $T$ is

  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/cfe398e1ab7e5b4b487671772bf4b6127e8e141b25491f96c5cc32e77869dec0.png)

We can check that the vertices of $R$ are mapped to the vertices of the parallelogram shown above as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
